name: LanceDB
tagline: Embedded, serverless retrieval database on the Lance columnar format for multimodal AI data.
description: LanceDB is a Rust retrieval engine built on Lance, an open columnar file format designed for ML data with fast random access and versioning. The open-source library runs embedded in Python, TypeScript or Rust and reads directly from local disk or object storage, so there is no server to run; LanceDB Cloud and Enterprise add a serverless/distributed service and a 'multimodal lakehouse' for feature engineering. It supports vector, full-text (BM25) and scalar-indexed search, zero-copy schema evolution and time travel across table versions. Especially strong when the same data feeds training pipelines and retrieval.

pricing.notes: Open-source library is free. LanceDB Cloud is usage-based serverless; LanceDB Enterprise (BYOC/managed, multimodal lakehouse) via sales.

scale.notes: OSS scales with storage (local or S3/GCS/Azure); Enterprise distributes query and indexing across nodes for billions of rows.

strengths: No server: embed it and point it at local disk or object storage
Lance format is efficient for both training scans and random-access retrieval
Versioned tables with time travel and zero-copy column additions
Vector, BM25 full-text and scalar indexes together
Handles images, video and other blobs alongside embeddings
weaknesses: Concurrent writers to the same table need care in OSS
Fast-moving 0.x API with frequent breaking changes
Distributed serving is a paid Cloud/Enterprise feature
Object-storage latency can hurt tail latency without caching
useCases: Embedded RAG in desktop, CLI and agent apps
Multimodal datasets shared by training and retrieval
notIdealFor: Teams wanting a classic client-server DB they can SSH into
